column1: # Vendored PUC 5.4.9 suite files that mention the internal test library T.
# Neither arm has the PUC ltests hooks (ltests.c, -DLUA_USER_H='"ltests.h"').
# "run" keeps such a file in the corpus: its T uses are all inside
# `assert(not T or ...)`, `if T then ... end` or an early
# `if T == nil then ... return end`, so with T undefined those blocks are dead
# code in both arms and only the rest of the file is compared -- the T-guarded
# blocks are skipped, not the file. "skip" keeps the documented SKIP with the
# reason below. A file moves to "run" only once every failure it shows is
# classified: a defect in tests/known-bad.tsv, a difference in
# tests/known-different.tsv with its docs/DIFFERENCES.md entry, or a skip row.

column3: T-guarded itself, but it is the suite driver: it loads and runs every other suite file and prints PUC's own summary, so the harness would run the corpus twice without comparing one feature
uses T.testC unguarded from line 31: the file is a testC harness, nothing left to compare without the PUC test library
uses T.listk and T.listcode unguarded (lines 38, 91): the file inspects PUC's constant and code lists

no T use outside a guard; the C-call bound it needs exists (tests/d54/err_12_ccall_reentry.lua). The printed stack-overflow depths differ by implementation limit: rows in tests/known-different.tsv
